cues.en: There's a lot of talk about sending humans to Mars, but no one talks about Venus.
cues.zh: 关于把人类送上火星的讨论很多，却没人谈论金星。

cues.en: Why not? And could Venus actually be the better option for a human colony?
cues.zh: 为什么？金星真的会是人类殖民的更好选择吗？

cues.en: Going to Mars has been a fixture in our collective cultural consciousness for a very long time. It's inspired more sci fi movies and stories than I can count, a ride at Disney World, and a Twitter following for the Mars Rover that's almost 2,000,000 strong.
cues.zh: 火星之旅长期以来一直是我们集体文化意识中的固定主题。它启发了数不清的科幻电影和故事、迪士尼世界的一个游乐项目，以及火星探测器在Twitter上近200万粉丝的关注。

cues.en: Meanwhile, Venus has inspired
cues.zh: 与此同时，金星激发了

cues.en: what?
cues.zh: 什么？

cues.en: Two Ray Bradbury stories,
cues.zh: 两篇雷·布拉德伯里的故事，

cues.en: a plant that eats flies, and a razor?
cues.zh: 一株吃苍蝇的植物，还有一把剃刀？

cues.en: Basically, Venus has the worst public relations team in the solar system. And that hurts our sister planet, not just in culture and media, but in space policy.
cues.zh: 基本上，金星拥有太阳系最糟糕的公关团队。而这伤害了我们的姐妹星球，不仅在文化和媒体方面，还在太空政策上。

cues.en: Presidents Bush and Obama and the Chinese government have all outlined goals for manned missions to Mars. The Dutch nonprofit group Mars One even held an international competition to find volunteers for a one way mission in the Martian surface. But Venus,
cues.zh: 布什总统、奥巴马总统和中国政府都提出了载人登陆火星的目标。荷兰非营利组织火星一号甚至举办了一场国际竞赛，招募志愿者参加火星表面单程任务。但金星，

cues.en: no manned mission love at all,
cues.zh: 完全没有载人任务的关爱，

cues.en: which is odd since in most respects, Venus is actually an easier and less costly colonization target than Mars is. For starters, Venus is closer to Earth. That's why we sent probes to Venus long before we sent them to Mars and why we sent more of them. Depending on the launch window, the round trip could be 30 to 50% shorter, which is a major factor for manned missions. Shorter trips means less weightlessness and radiation, less food and water to carry, and thus less fuel and lower cost. This would also be a huge advantage in moving the people and equipment necessary to colonize another world because bear in mind, there's no Craigslist in space. If we ever start a colony, we'll need to bring along almost everything.
cues.zh: 这很奇怪，因为在大多数方面，金星实际上比火星更容易、成本更低的殖民目标。首先，金星离地球更近。这就是为什么我们早在发送火星探测器之前就向金星发送了探测器，而且发送的数量更多。根据发射窗口的不同，往返行程可能缩短30%到50%，这是载人任务的一个主要因素。更短的行程意味着更少的失重和辐射，更少的食物和水要携带，因此更少的燃料和更低的成本。这也将是运送殖民另一个世界所需的人员和设备的巨大优势，因为请记住，太空中没有Craigslist。如果我们真的开始建立殖民地，我们几乎需要带上一切。

cues.en: And it's not just the shorter trip. The planet itself has some significant advantages over Mars. It's closer to the sun, which means about four times more available solar power than you have on Mars. It also has a thick atmosphere,
cues.zh: 而且不只是路程更短。这颗行星本身相比火星也有几项明显优势。它离太阳更近，这意味着可用的太阳能大约是火星上的四倍。它还有浓厚的大气层，

cues.en: unlike that wispy layer on Mars. That means better protection from space radiation and meteorites for our enterprising colonizers and their future cities. It also means more available carbon dioxide, from which, in principle, you might extract oxygen.
cues.zh: 不像火星上那层稀薄的大气。这意味着对我们勇于开拓的殖民者和他们未来的城市来说，能更好地抵御太空辐射和陨石。这也意味着有更多可用的二氧化碳，原则上可以从中提取氧气。

cues.en: But the real kicker is gravity. Venus has about 0.9 Earth g's, pretty close, while Mars has less than 0.4. And one thing we do know is that prolonged low gravity is bad for humans. How bad? In Earth orbit, astronauts lose bone mass at about 10 times the rate of someone with advanced osteoporosis.
cues.zh: 但真正关键的是重力。金星的重力约为地球的0.9倍，相当接近，而火星则不到0.4倍。我们已知的一件事是，长期低重力对人体有害。有多严重？在地球轨道上，宇航员骨质流失的速度大约是严重骨质疏松患者的10倍。

cues.en: Now, no one knows exactly how bad Martian gravity would be for humans, but it's definitely not gonna be good.
cues.zh: 目前，没人确切知道火星重力对人体会有多糟糕，但肯定好不了。

cues.en: On Venus, that's far less of a concern. And remember, we're talking about long term colonization,
cues.zh: 在金星上，这就远没那么令人担忧了。记住，我们说的是长期殖民，

cues.en: not just visits.
cues.zh: 而不只是造访。

cues.en: Even if we have the technological means to add water to a planet's surface and oxygen to its air, changing a planet's surface gravity is currently not even within the realm of discussion. So terraforming
cues.zh: 即便我们有技术手段为行星表面添水、为大气添氧，改变行星表面重力目前甚至都不在讨论范围内。所以地球化改造

cues.en: seems silly if people couldn't live there more than a few months without their bones falling apart. A theoretical Venusian colony thus seems to have a lot going for it. So why then this tunnel vision for Mars?
cues.zh: 如果人们在那儿待不了几个月骨头就散架了，那似乎很愚蠢。因此，理论上的金星殖民地看来优势不少。那么，为何还这般一门心思盯着火星呢？

cues.en: Surfacism.
cues.zh: 表面主义。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: I just made that word up, but hear me out.
cues.zh: 这个词是我刚编的，但听我说完。

cues.en: Ever since the days of seafaring exploration, we've had an obsession with landing on the surface of things. If you don't plant a flag on something, it's almost like having gotten there doesn't count. So what's all this have to do with Venus, which actually has a solid surface? Well, it does, but humans can't land on it. See, there's a teensy problem with temperature. There's so much CO two on Venus that the greenhouse effect makes the surface hotter than hell,
cues.zh: 自从航海探索时代以来，我们就痴迷于登陆事物的表面。如果你没在某个东西上插上旗帜，那几乎就等于没到过那里。那么这一切跟金星有什么关系呢？金星其实是有固体表面的。没错，确实有，但人类没法登陆上去。看，温度方面有个小问题。金星上的二氧化碳太多了，温室效应让表面热得跟地狱一样，

cues.en: over 450
cues.zh: 超过450

cues.en: degrees Celsius, well above the melting point of lead.
cues.zh: 摄氏度，远高于铅的熔点。

cues.en: But the bigger problem is the barometric pressure on the surface. It's over 90 Earth atmospheres.
cues.zh: 但更大的问题是地表的氣压，超过90个地球大气压。

cues.en: That means that landing on the Venusian surface would be like diving one kilometer underwater on Earth, far beyond the crushed depth of most military submarines.
cues.zh: 这意味着在金星地表着陆，相当于在地球水下1000米潜水，远远超过大多数军用潜艇的耐压极限。

cues.en: In fact, most probes that NASA and the Soviets sent to the surface of Venus imploded in mid air. We learned our lesson and a few reinforced probes did manage to touch down and send images of the Venusian surface, but even those only lasted about two hours before,
cues.zh: 事实上，NASA和苏联向金星地表发送的大多数探测器都在半空中内爆了。我们吸取了教训，少数加固过的探测器确实成功着陆并传回了金星地表的图像，但即便是那些也只坚持了大约两个小时，然后，

cues.en: you know. The point is, I think surfaceism is a real bias, and the fact that we can't live on the Venusian surface could help explain why Mars gets all the hype. But maybe that's sensible. I mean, if the surface will kill us, there's no point in going there. Right? Not so fast.
cues.zh: 你知道的。重点是，我认为“地表主义”是一种真实的偏见，而我们无法在金星地表生存这一事实，或许有助于解释为什么火星获得了所有的炒作。但也许这是合理的。我的意思是，如果地表会要我们的命，去那里就没有意义。对吧？别急。

cues.en: See, around 50 kilometers or 30 miles above the Venusian surface, some interesting things happen. First, the temperature drops to only about 70 degrees Celsius. That's still super hot, but firefighting equipment on Earth can withstand proximity to forest fires with temperatures that reach over 2,000 degrees Celsius.
cues.zh: 你看，在金星表面上方约50公里或30英里处，会发生一些有趣的事情。首先，温度降到只有约70摄氏度。这仍然超级热，但地球上的消防设备能承受接近森林大火的高温，那温度可达2000摄氏度以上。

cues.en: The pressure altitude also drops to almost exactly one Earth atmosphere.
cues.zh: 气压高度也几乎正好降到1个地球大气压。

cues.en: That means humans would need heat resistant clothing and oxygen masks, but not spacesuits to walk around in that environment. Granted, there's a minor nuisance of sulfuric acid floating around in the Venusian air, but that's potentially manageable. And at that altitude, the atmosphere is still dense enough for lots of stuff to float,
cues.zh: 这意味着人类需要耐热服和氧气面罩，但不需要宇航服就能在那样的环境中行走。当然，金星大气中飘浮着硫酸，这是个小小的麻烦，但或许可以应付。而在那个高度，大气仍然足够稠密，能让很多东西漂浮起来，

cues.en: like balloons filled with helium or maybe filled even with just regular Earth air.
cues.zh: 就像装满氦气的气球，甚至可能只装满普通的地球空气。

cues.en: Throw in the favorable gravity, and it starts to look like the upper atmosphere of Venus might be closest thing in the solar system to an Earth like environment.
cues.zh: 再加上有利的重力条件，看起来金星的上层大气可能是太阳系中最接近地球环境的地方。

cues.en: So it might make sense to colonize Venus with
cues.zh: 所以，用云城来殖民金星也许是合理的。

cues.en: cloud cities.
cues.zh: 云城。

cues.en: I am not making this up. NASA's Systems Analysis and Concepts
cues.zh: 我不是在编造这个。NASA的系统分析与概念团队

cues.en: has unveiled a conceptual blueprint for this scheme. They call it the High Altitude
cues.zh: 已经公布了这个方案的概念蓝图。他们称之为高空

cues.en: Venus Operational Concept or HAVOC.
cues.zh: 金星运营概念，简称HAVOC。

cues.en: Interesting branding choice, but still super awesome. We've linked the NASA videos in the description. You should check them out. Now for the record, this is all still conceptual. We are very far from sending this guy to lead our Venusian Cloud City, but NASA is taking the idea seriously.
cues.zh: 有趣的品牌选择，但依然超级棒。我们在简介里放了NASA视频的链接，你们应该去看看。不过要说明一下，目前这些都还只是概念。距离把这家伙送去领导我们的金星云城还差得远，但NASA正在认真对待这个想法。

cues.en: Right now, most of the chatter is still about using Venus as practice for colonies elsewhere like Mars. So we haven't overcome surfaceism just yet,
cues.zh: 眼下，大部分讨论还是把金星当作去火星等其他地方殖民的练习场。所以我们还没能克服“表面主义”，

cues.en: but this might change. The gravity issue alone might make Venus the go to option for long term human habitation.
cues.zh: 但这可能会改变。单是重力问题，就可能让金星成为人类长期居住的首选。

cues.en: Who knows? Centuries from now, if we learn how to sequester enough carbon out of its atmosphere, we might even be able to plant a flag or two. So what do you guys think? Is Venus a better colonization option than Mars?
cues.zh: 谁知道呢？几百年后，如果我们学会从金星大气中封存足够的碳，说不定还能插上一两面旗帜。那么你们怎么看？金星是比火星更好的殖民选择吗？

cues.en: Put your 2¢ in the comments, or even better, tweet them. Hashtag occupy Venus.
cues.zh: 在评论区说说你的看法，或者更好的是，发推文。标签：占领金星。

cues.en: If we start a grassroots movement, I'll let you know on the next episode of Space Time. Last week, we asked how you measure the size of the universe. Here were some of your questions. Optismi asked, how can space be expanding faster than light if the speed of light is the ultimate speed limit? I'm going answer you in two parts. First, the speed of light speed limit is for things moving through space, not about expansion of space itself. But second, you're right. I shouldn't be talking about space expanding at a given speed. I should be talking about the size of the enlarge setting on a photocopier button. If I hit enlarge once every second, then there will always be two points on the page that, if they're far enough apart to begin with, will end up more than one extra light second apart after I hit that photocopier button. Lingwingxing commented that this was a pretty intuitive way to understand inflation. Thanks for compliment, but be careful. We're talking about expansion of space in general. Inflation refers to a very specific expansion of space that occurred in just the first few instance after the Big Bang. TheMatman1313
cues.zh: 如果我们发起一场草根运动，我会在下一期《太空时光》里告诉大家。上周，我们问大家如何测量宇宙的大小。以下是你们的一些问题。Optismi问，如果光速是终极速度极限，空间怎么能比光速膨胀得更快？我分两部分回答你。第一，光速极限是针对在空间中运动的物体，而不是空间本身的膨胀。但第二，你说得对。我不该说空间以某个速度膨胀。我该说的是复印机上放大按钮的尺寸设定。如果我每秒按一次放大，那么页面上总会有两个点，如果它们一开始相距足够远，在我按下复印机按钮后，它们之间的距离会多出超过一光秒。Lingwingxing评论说，这是理解暴胀的一个相当直观的方式。谢谢夸奖，但要小心。我们说的是空间的一般膨胀。暴胀指的是大爆炸后最初几个瞬间发生的一种非常特定的空间膨胀。TheMatman1313

cues.en: says that the Hubble Bubble is a possible alternative to the idea that space is expanding at all. That's not correct. Space is expanding, period. What the Hubble bubble offers is a potential alternative
cues.zh: 说哈勃气泡可能是空间压根没有膨胀这一观点的一种替代解释。这不对。空间确实在膨胀，就这么简单。哈勃气泡提供的是一种潜在替代方案，

cues.en: to the currently observed accelerated expansion of space. Look it up. And to Brandon Spears, sure, we could always use help here at space time. Like the Hubble Space Telescope, we got schmutz on our lens too. So give it a wipe and help us out.
cues.zh: 用来解释目前观测到的空间加速膨胀。去查查吧。还有布兰登·斯皮尔斯，当然，我们《时空》节目随时欢迎帮手。就像哈勃太空望远镜一样，我们镜头上也有污渍。所以擦一擦，帮我们一把。
